div.l: And ȝit this Maunciple sette he alther cappe
The Reue was a sclender colrik man
His berd was shaue as nygh as eủere he can
His her was by his eres ful rounde y shorne
His top was dokked lyk a preest biforne
Ful longe were his legges and ful lene
Y lyk a staf . ther was no calf y sene
Wel cowthe he kepe a gerner or a bynne
Ther was non auditour / cowthe on hym wynne
Wel wiste he by the droughte and by the reyne
The ȝeldynge of his seed / and of his greyne
His lordes sheep his neet his dayerie
His swyn his hors his store and his pulletrie
Was holy in this Reues goủernynge
And by his couenant / ȝaf the reknynge
Syn that his lord was twenty ȝere of age
Ther cowthe no man / brynge hym in arrerage
Ther nas baily . heerde nor other hyne
That he ne knew his sleighte and his covyne
They were a drad of hym as of the deth
His wonynge was ful faire vpon an heth
With grene trees shadwed was his place
He cowthe better than his lord purchace
Ful riche he was astored pⁱriuely
His lord he cowthe wel plesen subtily
To ȝeue and lene him of his owne good
And haue a thank / and ȝit a coote and hood
In ȝowthe he hadde lerned a good mistere
He was a wel good wrighte a carpentere
This Reue sat vpon a ful good stot
That was al pomely grey / and highte Scot
A long surcote of peers vpon he hadde
And by his side he bar a rusty bladde
Of norfolk was this Reue of which I telle
Biside a toıı̄un men clepe Baldeswelle
Tukked he was as is a frere aboute
And eủere he rode the hinderest of oure route
A Sompnoᵘur was ther with vs in þᵗat place
That hadde a firy cherubinnes face
